SYNTHETIC DEMO
Dependency failure testing

Northstar / fragile checkout

Which user journeys survive when a geographic or network dependency group becomes unavailable? These are the observed results of controlled browser experiments.

Synthetic labels. Real browser failures.

Country and ASN labels in this run are assigned fixtures, not measured IP geolocation. Requests are genuinely aborted in Chromium; functional results and screenshots are captured from those runs.

04 / SCOPE & METHOD

Read the result precisely

What was tested

Baseline response addresses selected exact dependency origins. Later runs aborted HTTP(S) requests to those origins inside an isolated Chromium context. The same journey steps and browser settings were used throughout. Service workers were blocked and routing disabled the browser HTTP cache in both phases.

Protected origins: http://127.0.0.1:45189

What this does not prove

Country labels are not physical-location guarantees. CDN edges, anycast, proxies and DNS changes limit interpretation. These experiments do not reproduce a real national outage, measure data residency, inspect hidden backend dependencies, or prove causation or total application resilience. A PASS applies only to the tested assertions.

Privacy and credentials

Network evidence retains origins and IPs, not request paths, queries, headers or bodies. Error text is best-effort redacted; screenshots and application output can still contain sensitive information. Use staging and synthetic accounts. Console collection is enabled for this run.

Reproducibility

Schema 1 · Node v22.16.0 · 2 baseline attempt(s) and 1 scenario attempt(s) per relevant journey. Machine-readable evidence is saved alongside this report as report.json. This HTML embeds its screenshots and needs no server or external assets.
